comments.text: That music idea, it might seem silly now but it's an incredibly proof of concept. I was thinking there should be a webcam to MIDI generator, that operates somewhat like a theremin.  ie. track one had for volume and the other tracks the SHAPE of the other hand for notes (the wireframe indicates this is very likely to be possible), essentially requiring learning a sign language for notes (ie. 12 figures),and the y axis could be what octave the note occurs at, low-mid-high position could make a 3-octave range, maybe more... x-axis, maybe a vibrato with a calibration for center.   Once you're generating the notes it can be sent to high quality soundbanks/programs, so the fact it's just a basic sound now is of little significance, though many will judge it on that.

comments.author: @ubuenglish
comments.text: You should try using an AI to code a markdown to json parser. I have a feeling that the kind of games your building have been around since Pac Man and are probably relatively easy to solve for an AI. However, for more innovative or complex tasks, what AI need is a documentation and testing framework that the AI can follow to resolve issues and reach the coding goals.   AI assistants can be phenomenal in the right hands (not mine unfortunately). Benchmark tasks, like coding a snake game, tend to result in overestimation of the actual capabilities of AI programming, but if you're a developer, using AI can lead to 50% productivity gains. It's not over for coders, it's like you said about NVIDIA chips - more efficient coding just leads to more coding projects. Let's hope so anyway.
